clue.text: Writer in bed overwhelmed by endless lovemaking

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is cut away
to be overwhelmed is to be swamped on all sides, so one piece sits engulfed within another

parts.note: lovemaking is SEX, cut short to its first two letters
a crib is a child's bed

explanation.surface: An author tucked up in bed, swept away by a romantic encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bed' reads as one phrase, but 'in' only links the definition to the wordplay. 'endless' trims the last letter of the lovemaking word before it wraps around the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is someone who writes, historically a copyist of manuscripts, so the noun is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: They try to stop drag queen stuffing booty

indicators.note: stuffing is something packed inside, so one piece is pushed into the middle of another

parts.note: spoils are plunder or loot taken from an enemy
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Something that might stop a drag queen padding her bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag queen' looks like a single phrase from cabaret, but 'drag' belongs to the definition, meaning air resistance, and 'queen' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoilers on cars and aircraft disrupt airflow, and car spoilers are designed to manage turbulence and resistance behind the vehicle.

clue.text: Racketeer pilots a new car in reverse

parts.note: the Royal Air Force, whose members are pilots
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: going in reverse means travelling backwards, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: Lada is a Russian make of car

explanation.surface: A gangster's getaway drivers back a new car out of the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: A racketeer is normally a criminal; here it is someone who wields a racket, the Spanish tennis champion RAFA NADAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis player swings a racket, so a whimsical coinage turns the gangster word into a description of the sporting star.

clue.text: Amount offered to kidnap right-winger

indicators.note: kidnapping means seizing and holding someone captive, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a bid is the sum offered at an auction
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A ransom offered by kidnappers who have seized a right-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right-winger' reads as a political conservative; split at the hyphen, 'right' gives R and 'winger' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything with wings can whimsically be called a winger, and a bird is the obvious creature that flies on them.

clue.text: Everything screened by broadcaster is more jaundiced

indicators.note: something screened is shielded behind a cover, so one piece is shut inside another

parts.note: a sower scatters, or broadcasts, seed by hand
all means everything

explanation.surface: Watching everything a TV channel shows leaves a viewer more cynical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcaster' points at television, but to broadcast originally meant to scatter seed widely, so the broadcaster is a SOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaundice turns skin yellow, and sallow describes an unhealthy yellowish complexion, so the comparative forms match.

clue.text: Ban this awful drink

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A temperance campaigner demands prohibition of a horrible beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Absinth, also spelt absinthe, was in fact banned in many countries for much of the twentieth century, which is why the surface fits so well.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a strong green anise-flavoured spirit, so it is one example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Behold Harry Potter crushing rubbish basket

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and push about, so the letters are knocked out of place

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
BS is the abbreviation of a vulgar word for nonsense
the surname rearranged

explanation.surface: Look: the boy wizard is squashing a wastepaper basket.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Potter is the boy wizard, but 'Harry' is a verb telling us to rearrange the surname. The rubbish is the abbreviation of a vulgar word for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster pot is a wicker or mesh trap used for catching shellfish, and it is basically a basket.

clue.text: See 29
Soldiers' mess showing The Magnificent Seven perhaps

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to make a hash of something is to make a mess of it

explanation.surface: The army canteen is screening a classic Western for the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' suggests a military dining hall, which fits soldiers; it actually means a muddle, HASH. 'perhaps' warns that the film is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magnificent Seven remade Kurosawa's Seven Samurai as a Western, and a reworking of old material is a typical remake or recycled version.

clue.text: Happy Monday afternoon coming up in wee outhouse

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: to go is a colloquial way of saying to wee

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Bez is the dancer and percussionist of the Manchester band Happy Mondays
A is an abbreviation for afternoon

explanation.surface: After a cheerful start to the week, someone relieves themselves in a little shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy Monday' reads as a cheerful start to the week, but it is a member of the band Happy Mondays. 'wee' looks like Scottish for small; it is the verb, giving GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small garden building or summerhouse, a structure standing apart from the main house.

clue.text: Deliveries cancelled before holidays

parts.note: an event that is called off is cancelled
breaks are short holidays

explanation.surface: Parcel drops were cancelled just before the holiday season.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliveries suggests parcels, but in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled; an off break is a ball that spins from the off side towards the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket every ball bowled is a delivery, and off breaks are a common kind of spin bowling.

clue.text: See 15
Secure country

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to obtain or win
second meaning: a nation or territory

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an adjective and noun, a safe nation; the verb sense of the first word is the one needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To land a job is to obtain it, and a land is a nation with its own territory and people.

clue.text: Gallery on board after controller returns to former position

indicators.note: coming after something means following it, so the piece mentioned first in the clue is placed second

parts.note: a rein controls a horse
on board a ship means within SS, the abbreviation for steamship, which wraps around the next piece
the Tate is a well-known London art gallery

explanation.surface: An art gallery's director is sacked and then brought back to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention: inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship. The clue says 'after controller', so the rein comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate someone is to restore them to an earlier job or rank, matching the verb with its object.

clue.text: Excessive noise worried uninitiated child at first

indicators.note: someone uninitiated has not been let in at the start, so the word loses its opening letter
placed at first means set at the very front of the sequence

parts.note: a child is a MINOR, here missing its first letter
a din is a loud noise
something that ate at you worried you

explanation.surface: A naive child is frightened by an overwhelming racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' looks like an anagram signal but it is ATE, as in 'it ate at him'. 'at first' moves the beheaded MINOR to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinate means beyond reasonable limits, an adjective meaning much the same as unreasonable or immoderate.

clue.text: Bum echoed Brando somewhere close to Los Angeles

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means poor or faulty, so the letters come out wrongly arranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A down-and-out repeats a famous Marlon Brando line, recalling his 'I coulda been a contender... instead of a bum' speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' looks like a noun, a tramp; it is an adjective meaning bad, telling us to rearrange the next two words. It is also a Patti Smith song on Horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Redondo Beach is a coastal city in Los Angeles County, California, a short drive south-west of downtown.

clue.text: Animals record released 50 years ago

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the four-legged creatures that people ride
second meaning: Patti Smith's debut album, released in November 1975

explanation.surface: A record about animals came out half a century ago.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the theme: Horses is Patti Smith's 1975 debut album, and several other answers are its tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses are hoofed mammals, and Horses is also the title of a celebrated punk-poetry LP from 1975.

clue.text: Nigel in Reform welcomes unusual form of protection delivering sorrowful lines

indicators.note: to reform is to remake into a new shape, so the letters are rebuilt
to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the name rearranged
EGIS is a rare variant spelling of aegis, meaning protection

explanation.surface: Nigel Farage's Reform party adopts an odd kind of security policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Reform UK is the British party led by Nigel Farage, which is the picture; here 'Reform' just means rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, so elegising is composing or reciting such a lament.

clue.text: Financier contracted Brazilian footballer within a day

indicators.note: something contracted has been shortened, so the word loses its last letter
within means inside, so one piece sits enclosed by the other

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday, one day
the Brazilian striker Neymar, shortened

explanation.surface: A backer signed up a Brazilian star in a deal done within a single day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' suggests signing a player, but it means shortened: NEYMAR loses his R and is placed inside MON.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneyman is someone who provides finance for a project, an informal word for a backer or investor.

clue.text: Tissue-wrapped gold halo

indicators.note: something wrapped is enclosed in a covering, so one piece is surrounded by another

parts.note: glia is the supporting tissue of the nervous system
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A golden halo kept safe in tissue paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tissue' suggests wrapping paper, but it is the biological sense: GLIA, nerve tissue. Gloria is also the opening track of Horses.
explanation.definitionFit: In art a gloria is a halo or aureole of light painted around a holy figure's head.

clue.text: One commanding batsman going up over mid-off

indicators.note: lying over something covers it, so one piece is wrapped around another
in a down answer, rising means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Brian Lara, the great West Indies batsman

indicators.note: something off has gone bad or is out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A dominant batsman lofts the ball over the fielder at mid-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-off is a cricket fielding position, but here 'mid' is the material and 'off' says to rearrange it. LARA wraps the result and the whole thing is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a senior naval officer who commands a fleet, so the phrase describes the rank.

clue.text: Secret love is nearby

definitions.note: adverb in the clue, prepositional phrase as the answer

parts.note: a closet desire is a secret one
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A hidden sweetheart lives just around the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: The break comes in an unexpected place: CLOSET plus O becomes CLOSE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Close to means near or not far from, the same idea of short distance as a neighbouring spot.

clue.text: Stop cat spending month inside box

indicators.note: inside means within, so one piece is enclosed by another
spending something means using it up, so those letters are lost

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for month
to cuff someone is to box their ears
a tomcat, TOM, without M

explanation.surface: A cat is stopped from spending a whole month stuck inside a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like a container for the cat, but it is the verb, to hit, giving CUFF; TOM minus M sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut off a supply or a speaker is to halt or interrupt it, a phrasal verb close to halt.

clue.text: Happy over credit increase

parts.note: being up means being cheerful
buying on tick means buying on credit

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased about a rise in their credit rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tick' is British slang for on credit. In a down clue 'over' means the first part sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An uptick is a small rise, especially in a market or statistic, so it is a noun synonym for a rise.

clue.text: Singer and model coming back with German opening track

indicators.note: to open something is to split it apart, so other letters are placed in the gap

parts.note: a path is a track

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A singer and a model return with a German to open an album track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer and model' looks like a two-part description of one person, but only 'Singer' defines; 'model' gives SIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Patti Smith is the American punk poet and vocalist whose album Horses is the puzzle's theme.

clue.text: Apostrophe is dividing corporation

indicators.note: dividing something means splitting it in two, so one piece goes into the middle of another

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, or tum
taken as written

explanation.surface: A punctuation mark is causing a split in a company.
explanation.walkthrough: Apostrophe looks like the punctuation mark, but it is the rhetorical device of addressing someone directly. Corporation meaning a big belly is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuism, from Latin tu meaning you, is direct address in the second person, the rhetorical sense of the word.

clue.text: 3 characters reflected in strange TikToks

definitions.note: a cross-reference to the answer of 3 down

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters run the other way
characters are letters, so the solution is found among the printed letters
found in means sitting among the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words, read backwards

explanation.surface: Three people show up in some weird social media videos.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' looks like a number but refers to 3 down, BIRD; the answer is spelt backwards across 'strangE TIKtoks'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is a bird of prey related to hawks, so it is an example of the creature named at the cross-reference.

clue.text: Independent bank promoting Head of Finance

indicators.note: to promote is to move up a rank, and in a down answer moving the opening letter of the money word up means shifting it to the top

parts.note: a reef is a bank of rock or sand near the surface of the sea

explanation.surface: A bank with no ties gives its finance chief a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' sounds financial, matching 'Finance', but it is a REEF; the F at its end is moved to the top of this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone free is not controlled or ruled by others, so the adjective is a plain synonym of self-governing.

clue.text: Cabaret singer loses face covering AC/DC in rave venue

indicators.note: losing one's face means losing the front, so the first letter goes
covering something means going all round it, so one piece is wrapped round another

parts.note: Liza Minnelli starred as the singer Sally Bowles in the film Cabaret
AC/DC is slang for bisexual, shortened to bi

explanation.surface: A cabaret singer is embarrassed while covering a rock band's song at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC looks like the Australian rock band; here it is the slang term for bisexual. LIZA loses her L and goes around BI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish Balearic island famous for its nightclubs and dance-music scene, so it is a party destination.

clue.text: Political doctrine on the subject of class is principle of Marxism

parts.note: re means concerning
a form is a school class
taken as written

indicators.note: the principal or chief part is the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A statement that class struggle is the central idea of Marxist theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principle' is a play on principal, meaning first; 'class' is a school form, which the British use for a year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Reformism is the belief that society should be changed gradually through reforms rather than revolution, a political ideology.

clue.text: Mike Batt wryly remixed Pussycat Doll

indicators.note: a remix reworks a recording into a new version, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The songwriter Mike Batt ironically reworks a track by a girl group.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Batt is a British songwriter, which makes 'remixed' look musical; 'wryly' is part of the material. Kimberly is also a song on Horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Kimberly Wyatt was a member of the American pop group the Pussycat Dolls, so the phrase names her band.

clue.text: Royal daughter hosting a president

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so one piece is received inside another

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare
taken as written

explanation.surface: A princess entertains a visiting head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal daughter' suggests a real princess, but it is Shakespeare's Regan, King Lear's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the fortieth President of the United States, so the answer is an example of the title.
